For example, I can experimentally find infinite families of combinatorial objects that describe a Fix(U^2) where U is some group action.

But when I try to prove it with Lean, I somehow encounter infinite regress issues, where recursive descent prevents me from handing cases for all n, m, p parameters, but instead I figure out a branch for 0, 0, 1 case, and then i continue and it's 0, 0, 2 case etc.

Is there some strategy which would allow me to get the recursion to just say it is n,m,p case of this particular family and I can deal with branches that deal with other families?

For example, usually what happens in completeness proofs is that some branches are a contradiction, which is easy to prove, but then I feel like again, I get infinite regress and have to prove it's a contradiction for every single case.

The funny thing is that I know exactly what the unique/complete structure is, yet somehow I cannot recover it from lean induction, even though it is a recursive structure.
It would be helpful to have a #mwe of what you want to do.

thanks, i'll try to actually prove it first, as i don't have a working example, i do have a bunch of proofs, but none that actually prove completeness or just 1 direction of implication (Fix(U^2) => my infinite families)

I have proofs that demonstrate U (U f) = f holds for my families, but that is not at all as hard as completeness (my families are the only families in Fix(U^2), no other families exist).

https://github.com/vjeranc/fixed-rtrt/

I managed to eventually capture the proof with integer params...
Just made a predicate that can fully capture integer runs.

but, there was also a "squeeze" operation which eliminates integers fully when traversing the proof, so integer parameterization can be skipped.

although the contradictions are still there, at first i thought it was just due to recursive mismatch of different structures defined in Lean, but it ended up being an actual iterated equation that I managed to capture in Lean as well. Instead of expanding infinitely the branches, reproving contradictions, having 1 branch remaining, and continuing regress again, it is also possible to just define this residual as well.

so i think i learned how to deal with this in lean, not that difficult.
